title: Held-out data registry for Track B and the open-population lane
purpose: The single registry of the data that every Track B gate and every open-population gate holds out, set up by the dynamics coordinator on 2026-10-21. It is part of Track B's B0.2 exposure record (design revision 3, section 5.2, elements 4 and 5). Cite it by path, commit and SHA-256. src/populace_dynamics/track_b/holdout_registry.py states and enforces its rules, and tests/test_track_b_holdout_registry.py runs them on every commit.
rules: A gate registers what it holds out here, as a lone candidate entry in a commit of its own, before its record freezes. It moves to frozen, used or withdrawn only in later commits.

J's candidate holdouts are registered first, because J is on Track B's critical path. OP0.2 registers its picks for OP12's gate_ssa_totals here before it freezes them, and picks from the years J has not taken.

Every unit key names a declared source, then its years (a year, an inclusive range, or 'undated'), then optional scope segments. Each source declares a family, a title, a catalog reference no other source shares, and what its key year means. A new source is added only if it is not another name for a declared one.

Two unit keys share a unit when their source is the same and their years intersect; scope segments describe the unit and never narrow the overlap. Live entries that share a unit list each other in disclosed_overlaps, and both gates' registrations name the overlap. No unit is held out by two gates silently.

The overlap rule cannot see two sources that share underlying data, or two editions of a publication that report the same data years. So an entry lists in overlap_review, with a reason, every earlier live entry of the same source family that it neither shares a unit with nor discloses.

Reference years are recorded separately from interview or publication availability (design section 5.2, element 10): a unit key's year is what its source declares (for PSID, the interview wave), and each entry's units state the reference or event years.

An entry whose gate has scored has status 'used'. Its scored_evidence cites committed artifacts of that run, each with a field whose value identifies the gate. Its units are exposure for every later gate and never again an unused holdout (design section 5.2).

Entries are only appended. An entry's id, provenance, gate, lane, source, units and unit_keys never change; its gate identifiers, evidence, scored evidence, disclosures, reviews and history only extend. Ids are never reused.
A historical import records a gate that froze or scored before this registry existed. Imports are allowed only while the registry is incomplete.

The registry is incomplete until completion_record, B0.2's mechanical exposure inventory, exists. It starts with the prior uses verified below; the inventory adds the rest before any B0.2 gate record freezes.

status_values.candidate: registered by a gate's B0.2 or OP0.2 record; not yet frozen
status_values.frozen: fixed in a frozen gate record before that gate's candidates run
status_values.used: scored by a registered gate; exposure for every later gate
status_values.withdrawn: released before use, with the reason recorded
